title: Coding Set 06: Special Numbers & GCD/LCM Reduction
description: Reported HCL number-crunching rounds: Armstrong/Strong/Perfect classification and array GCD & LCM.

problems.title: Classify Armstrong, Strong & Perfect Number
problems.statement: Given a positive integer N, check which of the following three properties hold for N: (1) ARMSTRONG: sum of each digit raised to the power of total digits equals N; (2) STRONG: sum of factorials of each digit equals N; (3) PERFECT: sum of proper divisors (< N) equals N. Print matching labels in order (ARMSTRONG, STRONG, PERFECT) separated by a single space, or 'NONE' if none apply.

testCases.note: 1^1 = 1 and 1! = 1; proper divisors of 1 sum to 0 != 1

starterCode.python:
import sys

n = int(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
# Write your solution here

edgeCases: N = 1: Armstrong & Strong, NOT Perfect (proper divisors sum is 0)
Perfect square divisor `d * d == n`: do not add `d` twice

problems.title: GCD & LCM of an Integer Array
problems.statement: Given N positive integers, compute both the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) and the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the entire array. Print '<GCD> <LCM>'.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated positive integers.
problems.outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: GCD and LCM.

starterCode.python:

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]

# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys, math

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
arr = data[1:1+n]
g = arr[0]
l = arr[0]
for v in arr[1:]:
    g = math.gcd(g, v)
    l = (l // math.gcd(l, v)) * v
print(f'{g} {l}')

edgeCases: Avoid intermediate overflow by computing `(l / gcd(l, v)) * v` instead of `(l * v) / gcd(l, v)`
